title: Brain-inspired AI and visual processing
text:
This is fascinating and shows where AI needs to go (mimicry of nature).

Scientists have created an extremely compact AI model inspired by the brain’s visual system using data from macaque monkey neurons (a team reports in the journal Nature). The original AI vision model had 60 million variables, but researchers compressed it to about 10,000 variables while maintaining similar performance. The result is a tiny, efficient model that behaves more like real brain neurons—particularly those in the V4 visual cortex, which recognize shapes, curves, colors, and textures.

The work suggests that biological brains achieve complex perception with far simpler and more efficient systems than today’s energy-intensive AI. Studying these compact, brain-like models could help scientists understand human brain function and diseases like Alzheimer’s, while also guiding the development of smaller, more efficient AI systems—for example in applications like self-driving cars.
